name: graph-rag
context: Knowledge-intensive tasks over large document collections where flat-text chunk retrieval misses relationships between entities. GraphRAG first extracts a knowledge graph from the corpus (entities, relationships), then computes community structures within the graph, generates community-level summaries, and answers user questions by first identifying relevant communities and then finding specific supporting evidence within those communities. This produces more comprehensive and semantically coherent answers than flat chunk retrieval.
benefits: Captures entity relationships that flat chunk retrieval misses
Community-structured summaries enable global question answering
Improved factual accuracy on knowledge-intensive tasks
tradeoffs: Graph construction is expensive (requires LLM entity extraction)
Higher latency than naive chunk retrieval
Tuning community detection parameters is non-trivial
use_cases: Answering questions about a legal document corpus
Technical documentation Q&A over a codebase
Financial report analysis over earnings filings
avoid_when: Small corpus where flat chunk retrieval suffices
Corpus is not parseable for entity extraction
anti_patterns: Skipping community structure and doing flat graph retrieval only
Using the same chunk size for entity extraction and final retrieval
No entity deduplication across the corpus
design_principles: Extract entities and relationships before building the graph index
Tune community detection for corpus size and entity density
Combine global community answers with local supporting evidence
best_practices: Use an LLM for entity and relationship extraction from each chunk
Apply community detection (e.g., Leiden algorithm) before summarization
Store both the community summaries and the raw community subgraph for answer grounding
references: Edge et al., From Local to Global: A GraphRAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization, 2024 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130
